   3.1 Tense cmavo (PU series) attach to the following selbri, not to sumti or to the name in a vocative:  
       - <invalid_quote>ba: default future tense; after [sumti]; will [selbri]</invalid_quote> (section-connected-tenses.txt).  
   3.2 In (B) “ba meris” attempts to treat “meris” as if it were the selbri or future predicate, but “meris” is a name (sumti) and cannot function as a selbri. Hence “ba” is stranded on a sumti with no predicate to govern its interpretation.  
   3.3 The only way to correctly mark future is “ba jemna” (with “jemna” as selbri) optionally followed by “la meris” as x2, or “ba … ba …” logical connections (Example 10.152–153).

   4.1 (B) cannot unambiguously mean “we will compete with Meris,” because the order suggests “we-we+you compete (now?) — future Meris.” Lojban demands clarity of x1, selbri, x2 in sequence: sumti–PU–selbri–sumti or sumti–selbri–PU–sumti.  
   4.2 (A) correctly places “jemna” then “ba” then a sumti, even though separated by a terminator, and would be salvaged by reinserting “la” and terminators. (B) omits necessary “do’u” when inserting DOI inside a bridi (section-elidable-terminators.txt).

   5.2 B’s claim that “ba meris” is future x2 ignores that a PU tense must immediately precede selbri (Example 10.153 splits into two bridi). They produce an orphaned PU with no brivla.  
   5.3 They insist absence of “ko” proves a statement not command, but this ignores that inserting DOI inside the bridi without “do’u” turns the entire sentence into a command to the bridi “doi jemna” if anything. Commands require “ko” in the sumti place, not DOI.  

6. Correct Alternative and Conclusion  
   6.1 A grammatical rendering would be:  
       “mi’o do’u doi la meris do’u jemna ba”  
       or simply place vocative at sentence end:  
       “mi’o jemna ba la meris doi.”  
   6.2 Sentence 8’s assertion that (B) is clear and grammatical ignores fundamental Lojban syntax for vocatives and tenses, resulting in ungrammatical and semantically vacuous output.

The bare selbri “jemna” functions like a descriptive vocative “the competitor” (an implicit “le jemna”).  
   2.2. Debater_A demands a full sumti after COI/DOI, but Example 6.67 shows even a bare selbri is allowed as description:

   3.1. Tense “ba” attaches to the bridi’s selbri-sumti complex immediately to its right. In (B) the selbri is “jemna” and x2 is “meris.” Thus “jemna ba meris” means “will compete with Meris.”  
     • <quote>ion: will [selbri]; after [sumti]; default future tense</quote> (section-10.20).  
     • Example 10.153: <invalid_quote>mi pu je ba klama</invalid_quote> shows “ba” marking the upcoming “klama.”  
   3.2. Debate_A’s claim that “ba meris” is orphaned ignores that “jemna ba meris” is one unit. There is no requirement that the name precede the selbri; sumti order in Lojban is flexible so long as the ga’o connectives are not sap. Here “x2” appears after “jemna,” the canonical sumti-after-selbri order, albeit with explicit tense on x2 but interpreted as tense for the bridi.  

4. Why (A) fails

   4.2. Splitting by period prohibits “ba” from attaching to the previous “jemna,” so no coherent future proposition.

   5.1. Debater_A insists on using “do'u” within a bridi, but “do'u” is only needed when a simple vocative word is placed “somewhere within a bridi” where ambiguity may arise. Here the vocative is at the bridi’s start and there is no ambiguity: the sentence boundary is clear.  
     • <quote>the elidable terminator for vocative phrases is __do'u__ (of selma'o DOhU), which is rarely needed except when</quote> (section-elidable-terminators.txt).  
   5.2. Standard practice omits “do'u” at the very beginning of an utterance, as in Example 6.66: <quote> djan.</quote>

   6.1. “mi’o” unambiguously refers to speaker+listener. No “ko” is present, so it is not a command.  
   6.2. The listener sees “doi jemna…” and understands “competitor, we and you will compete….”  
   6.3. Debater_A’s “mi’o do'u doi la meris do'u jemna ba do`u” is needlessly profligate; Lojban style favors brevity when unambiguous.
